 Guy Ritchie exploded onto the scene in 1998 with the release of the crime comedy Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels. Since then, he has been a staple in the genre, often mixing gritty drama with his penchant for deliciously dark humor. However, his first foray into fantasy happened almost a decade ago, and while it failed to launch a franchise, it has evolved into a streaming giant over the years. Now, the film continues to climb up the streaming charts and become a smash hit for Netflix .

 In 2017, Ritchie released his take on a fantasy epic with King Arthur: Legend of the Sword . While a financial and critical fop, it is now regarded as one of the filmmaker's most underrated titles. Featuring a star-studded cast led by Jude Law and Charlie Hunnam, the $175 million blockbuster followed the origins and rise of the legendary folk hero. Despite its scale, Ritchie still infused his filmmaking style, creating a jaw-dropping opening sequence followed by several exciting, CGI-heavy action set pieces. And it is clear streaming audiences still can't get enough.
 King Arthur: Legend of the Sword is currently available to stream on Netflix and in the first week of November, it pulled in 179 million minutes, according to Nielsen. It took the eighth spot on the Top 10 most-watched movies across all platforms, just above Home Alone (Disney+) and Collision Course (Netflix). Hitting the charts nearly a decade after its theatrical release is certainly an achievement, especially for a film like Legend of the Sword , which received mixed reviews and failed to break even at the box office.

 The Nielsen streaming numbers arrive after it was reported that Legend of the Sword reached the Top 10 list on Netflix itself, beating out Kidnapped in Her Own Home and Cry Macho at the eighth spot. Of course, the film has been on several platforms since its theatrical release in 2017, including on free streaming services like Tubi . It has been on and off Netflix over the years, but it never fails to reach the coveted charts.

 Despite King Arthur: Legend of the Sword regularly returning to the streaming charts, there has been no movement on the sequel since it flopped at the box office. Guy Ritchie and Warner Bros. had ambitious plans for a six-film franchise, but all were canceled soon after the lackluster results of the original. Still, despite the box office take and a low 31% score on Rotten Tomatoes, the film continues to prove that audiences are still more than happy taking a two-hour trip into the short-lived cinematic universe.
